ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. James Okafor, MD
Department: Cardiology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive difficulty walking with bilateral thigh and buttock pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with peripheral artery disease returns for cardiology evaluation three months after his January 2020 gastroenterology visit. He notes tightness and aching pain in his calves, thighs, and buttocks bilaterally after walking about 50 meters, which is relieved by resting for a few minutes. He has not seen a physician in several years.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Chronic pancreatitis (dietary management) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
- Tobacco use disorder
- Alcohol use disorder, severe
- Alcoholic cirrhosis
- Chronic pancreatitis
- Non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe
- Peripheral artery disease (aortoiliac occlusive disease/Leriche syndrome)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Ipratropium bromide inhaler 17 mcg, 2 puffs four times daily
- Aspirin 81 mg orally daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg orally daily
- Thiamine 100 mg orally daily
- Folic acid 1 mg orally daily
- Multivitamin 1 tablet orally daily
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 36,000 lipase units with meals and snacks
- Omeprazole 20 mg orally daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis
- Mother with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
- Brother with coronary artery disease

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He has a 30-pack-year smoking history

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
He reports no chest pain or shortness of breath

VITAL SIGNS:
His blood pressure is 138/84 mmHg, pulse is 76/min, and BMI is 27 kg/m²

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, dorsalis pedis and femoral pulses are markedly diminished bilaterally. There is loss of hair and coolness over both legs, with no skin ulcers. Mild weakness is noted in the lower limbs with reduced ankle reflexes bilaterally. Sensory testing shows decreased pinprick sensation over the feet.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-03-15
Provider: Dr. Robert Patel, MD
Department: Gastroenterology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fatigue, decreased appetite, abdominal discomfort, and yellowing of eyes

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to Gastroenterology with recurrent symptoms in the setting of known alcoholic cirrhosis and chronic pancreatitis, evaluated six months prior without jaundice. The wife has noticed yellowing of his eyes and increased irritability. He has also complained of diffuse muscle weakness and occasional nausea, but no vomiting or diarrhea. He denies abdominal trauma or recent travel. Over the past year, he has lost about 6 kg (13 lb) without trying.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Chronic pancreatitis (dietary management) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Leriche syndrome (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Alcoholic cirrhosis (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
- Alcoholic hepatitis (diagnosed 2021-09-15)
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
- Tobacco use disorder
- Alcohol use disorder, severe
- Chronic pancreatitis
- Peripheral artery disease (aortoiliac occlusive disease/Leriche syndrome)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Ipratropium bromide inhaler 17 mcg, 2 puffs four times daily
- Aspirin 81 mg orally daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg orally daily
- Thiamine 100 mg orally daily
- Folic acid 1 mg orally daily
- Multivitamin 1 tablet orally daily
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 36,000 lipase units with meals and snacks
- Omeprazole 20 mg orally daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Family history is notable for his father's death from myocardial infarction at age 63 and his mother's death from breast cancer at age 70.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
The patient works as a construction foreman and says his job is stressful, often leading him to have "a few beers" after work. On further questioning, he admits to drinking 8–10 beers daily for more than 25 years, with occasional whiskey on weekends. He smokes one pack of cigarettes per day and has done so for 30 years. His diet consists mainly of fast food and processed snacks, and he rarely exercises.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
Review of systems is notable for mild difficulty sleeping, decreased libido, and occasional easy bruising. There is no history of hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath.

VITAL SIGNS:
Vital signs: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 138/84 mm Hg, pulse 88/min, respirations 18/min. BMI is 27 kg/m².

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the patient appears tired but alert. There is mild scleral icterus, palmar erythema, and multiple spider angiomata over the upper chest and shoulders. The abdomen is soft but mildly distended, with a liver edge palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin; the liver is firm and mildly tender. Shifting dullness is absent. There is no splenomegaly. No peripheral edema is noted.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies show:
AST										178 U/L
ALT										 74 U/L
ALP										250 IU/L
GGT										 Elevated
Total bilirubin							 3.1 mg/dL
Albumin									Mildly decreased
INR										 Mildly prolonged
Hepatitis B and C serologies are negative.

IMAGING:
Abdominal ultrasound shows an enlarged liver with heterogeneous echotexture, no focal masses, and patent hepatic vessels.

PATHOLOGY:
A liver biopsy is performed to evaluate the degree of inflammation and fibrosis. Histopathology demonstrates swollen hepatocytes with ballooning degeneration, infiltration by neutrophils, and irregular, rope-like eosinophilic inclusions in the cytoplasm.
